boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, publicly documented destinations on practical campus-adjacent Birmingham corridors.

cards.title: Railroad Park
cards.subtitle: 1st Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Enter from 1st Avenue South and use the park’s walking paths, gardens, play areas, and water features for a self-directed outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A 19-acre public green space running along the railroad corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Railroad Park is a 19-acre greenspace on 1st Avenue South between 14th and 18th Streets, and public admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily, 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; the official site states there is no entrance fee.

cards.title: Regions Field
cards.subtitle: 1st Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Check the Birmingham Barons schedule before going; the ballpark’s main public-facing location is on 1st Avenue South across from Railroad Park.
cards.short_summary: The downtown home field of the Birmingham Barons.
cards.evidence_claim: Regions Field, at 1401 1st Avenue South, is home to the Birmingham Barons and is in downtown’s Parkside District.
cards.access_notes: Game and event access depends on the published schedule and ticket availability.

cards.title: Negro Southern League Museum
cards.subtitle: 16th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum stop to explore Birmingham’s connection to Black baseball history; confirm the posted hours before travel.
cards.short_summary: A city museum focused on the Negro Southern League and Birmingham Black Barons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Negro Southern League Museum at 120 16th Street South presents the history and impact of African-American baseball.
cards.source_title: City of Birmingham — Negro Southern League Museum
cards.access_notes: The city lists museum hours Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Red Mountain Theatre
cards.subtitle: 3rd Avenue South corridor
cards.notes: Look over the current program and choose a Mainstage or Discovery Theatre performance that fits your schedule before purchasing tickets.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit performing-arts campus with two named theatres.
cards.evidence_claim: Red Mountain Theatre’s Arts Campus at 1600 3rd Avenue South includes the RMT Mainstage and the 133-seat Discovery Theatre.
cards.access_notes: Performance and box-office timing varies by production; consult the theatre’s current calendar.

cards.title: Alabama Theatre
cards.subtitle: 3rd Avenue North corridor
cards.notes: Use the theatre’s event calendar to select a film, concert, or live performance, then arrive via its documented 3rd Avenue North address.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown venue presenting films and live performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alabama Theatre is at 1817 Third Avenue North and has presented movies, concerts, and live performances since 1927.
cards.access_notes: Events are individually scheduled; tickets are offered through the theatre’s event listings.

cards.title: McWane Science Center
cards.subtitle: 19th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Visit during daytime museum hours and use the center’s floor maps to plan exhibits and programming around the 2nd Avenue North corner.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit science museum and research center in downtown Birmingham.
cards.evidence_claim: McWane Science Center is a science museum and research center at 200 19th Street North, on the corner of 2nd Avenue North.
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours are weekdays 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.

cards.title: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
cards.subtitle: 16th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Set aside time for the institute’s galleries and use the 15th Street North entrance for the free parking described by the museum.
cards.short_summary: A museum destination within Birmingham’s Civil Rights District.
cards.evidence_claim: The Birmingham Civil Rights Institute is located at 520 16th Street North and provides parking access from 15th Street North.
cards.access_notes: Check the institute’s current tour hours and admissions information before visiting.

cards.title: Sixteenth Street Baptist Church
cards.subtitle: 6th Avenue North corridor
cards.notes: Use the church’s official contact details to arrange an appropriate visit, and treat this active congregation and historic site with care.
cards.short_summary: A named historic church in the Civil Rights District.
cards.evidence_claim: Sixteenth Street Baptist Church lists its address as 1530 6th Avenue North in Birmingham.
cards.access_notes: Hours and visitor arrangements are not verified here; contact the church directly before going.

cards.title: Kelly Ingram Park
cards.subtitle: 17th Street North corridor
cards.notes: Walk the park’s monument grounds at your own pace and pair it with nearby Civil Rights District sites for historical context.
cards.short_summary: A city park whose monuments commemorate Birmingham civil-rights history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Birmingham identifies Kelly Ingram Park as a Civil Rights Movement battleground with monuments recognizing its history.
cards.access_notes: A City of Birmingham event notice places the park at 500 17th Street North and 5th Avenue North.

cards.title: Birmingham Public Library — Central
cards.subtitle: Park Place corridor
cards.notes: Bring a research question or browse the Central Library’s archives, manuscripts, and subject departments during its posted public service hours.
cards.short_summary: The central branch of Birmingham’s public-library system, with archives and research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Birmingham Public Library’s Central location is at 2100 Park Place and includes Archives and Manuscripts, arts, business, and other departments.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday and Wednesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–6 p.m.; Tuesday 9 a.m.–8 p.m.
